questions.title: Who will win the men's 5,000 metres at the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship in September 2026?
questions.background: The inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship is scheduled to take place in Budapest in September 2026.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : World Athletics' official results or contemporaneous reporting from a reputable news organization. Resolution : Resolve to the athlete declared the winner of the men's 5,000-metre final at the September 2026 World Athletics Ultimate Championship, once the final result is announced. Accepted Answer Format : The winning athlete's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major upgrade for Jakob Ingebrigtsen (0.22 -> 0.35), who erased post-Achilles surgery doubts by winning 5,000m gold at the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham on Aug 10 (13:15.29) in his first race in 324 days after only six weeks of full training (Reuters/HT Aug 11). With tune-up 1500m Diamond League races in Silesia (Aug 23) and Zurich (Aug 27) giving him another month to peak—and his Aug 14 remarks emphasizing full commitment to major championships—he is the clear favorite for Budapest's unpaced 12-man 5,000m final. Reigning World 5,000m champion Cole Hocker trims slightly (0.23 -> 0.20) as FloTrack (Aug 17) notes he still faces a choice between the 1500m and 5000m in Budapest, with 24% left outside the top 5 (including Monaco DL winner Dominic Lobalu, Graham Blanks, Andreas Almgren, Nico Young, and Ethiopian/Kenyan qualifiers).

questions.title: Who will win the men's javelin throw at the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship in September 2026?
questions.background: The inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship is scheduled to take place in Budapest, Hungary, in September 2026.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : World Athletics' official results for the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship. Resolution : Resolve to the athlete awarded the men's javelin throw gold medal at the conclusion of the competition in September 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The winning athlete's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 57-day refresh ahead of Lausanne DL (Aug 21), Zurich DL (Aug 27), Brussels DL Final (Sept 4-5), and Budapest's 8-man Ultimate Championship (cut-down format unveiled Aug 20: 8->6->4 after two attempts): (1) Sri Lanka's Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage surges 0.28 -> 0.35 after winning 8 of 9 meets in 2026, adding Commonwealth Games gold on Aug 1 with 89.75m atop his 92.62m Rome world lead and leading Diamond League standings (23 pts, already qualified). (2) Germany's Julian Weber jumps 0.17 -> 0.25 after unleashing a massive 90.40m European Championship record in Birmingham on Aug 15-16—becoming the only other 90m+ thrower in 2026 (capped at 0.25 pending check on his Lausanne withdrawal, likely post-Euros rest). (3) Two-time world champion Anderson Peters holds 0.14 (2nd in DL standings with 22 pts, healthy and qualified). (4) Neeraj Chopra drops sharply 0.16 -> 0.09: post-lower-back injury form remains capped at 85.83m SB (CWG silver, admitting 'fitness is not like before') AND Outlook India (Aug 20) reports he sits 9th in Ultimate Championship standings—outside the top-8 Sept 1 cutoff with genuine non-qualification risk. (5) Arshad Nadeem is removed (0.09 -> ~0.03) amid a severe slump (9th at CWG with 75.39m/77.41m, 9th in Lucerne 78.47m, withdrew from Lausanne), replaced at #5 by World #2 this season and 2025 World bronze medalist Curtis Thompson (0.065), leaving 10.5% for auto-qualified World champ Keshorn Walcott (~0.045), Nadeem (~0.03), and Jakub Vadlejch/field.

questions.title: Who will win the women's javelin title at the 2026 World Athletics Ultimate Championship in Budapest?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the athlete declared the women's javelin champion at the 2026 World Athletics Ultimate Championship in Budapest, according to the official World Athletics results. Resolution Date : 2026-09-19 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the athlete's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major upgrade for 18-year-old Chinese prodigy Yan Ziyi (0.34 -> 0.57) and plain ASCII fix for Adriana Vilagos. Since June 24, Yan extended her undefeated Diamond League streak to four wins—67.44m in Paris on June 28 (beating Vilagos 63.83m and Kitaguchi 63.01m, while world champ Juleisy Angulo finished last; SCMP) and 68.75m in Monaco on July 10 (Reuters), giving her four marks from 67.11m to 71.74m. Meanwhile, European rivals underwhelmed at the Aug 16 European Championships in Birmingham, where Sara Kolak won gold with just 62.43m (Straits Times), underscoring Yan's massive 5m+ superiority. We cap Yan at 0.57 pending formal Budapest entry confirmation (given late-September Asian Games proximity) and inherent javelin event variance, leaving 10% outside the top 5 (Sigrid Borge, Sara Kolak, Victoria Hudson, Juleisy Angulo).

questions.title: Who will win the men's 200m at the 2026 World Athletics Ultimate Championship?
questions.background: The inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship is scheduled for September 11–13, 2026, in Budapest.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official World Athletics results, supported by contemporaneous reporting of the championship. Resolution : Resolve to the athlete who wins the men's 200m final at the 2026 Ultimate Championship, scheduled for September 11–13, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The winning athlete's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: 57-day refresh incorporating July-August sprint results and Aug 20 Ultimate Championship format news: (1) Four-time defending World 200m champion Noah Lyles rises 0.41 -> 0.44 after scorching a world-leading 9.79s 100m at US Championships (July 24), serving as World Athletics' 'Ultimate MC' with explicit commitment to win Budapest, and gaining a direct tactical edge from the Aug 20 'lane draft' rule letting top-ranked sprinters pick their semifinal heat and lane (tempered slightly by his July 26 US 200m final hamstring cramp, which he called 'just cramp' after running two 9.7s). (2) Auto-qualified Olympic champion Letsile Tebogo trims 0.24 -> 0.22 after losing the July 4 Prefontaine Classic 200m in 19.93s (-0.9 wind). (3) Kenny Bednarek holds 0.14 (3rd in US 100m, skipped US 200m to stay fresh for late-season championships). (4) Gout Gout is REMOVED (0.03 -> 0.00) after tearing his left hamstring in July and ending his 2026 season (Reuters July 9). (5) Jamaican 19.6x threat Bryan Levell (0.045) and 18-year-old American sensation Tate Taylor (0.04, stunned Tebogo at Prefontaine in 19.75s into a -0.9 headwind, discounted modestly for top-16 ranking qualification uncertainty) round out the top 5 at 0.885, leaving 11.5% for Alexander Ogando, Makanakaishe Charamba, Courtney Lindsey, Garrett Kaalund, Zharnel Hughes, and the field.

questions.title: Which Brazilian Supreme Court justice, if any, will order Federal Police chief Andrei Rodrigues suspended during September 2026?
questions.background: Brazil’s Federal Police investigates federal crimes, and its leadership can be subject to judicial orders.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Public orders from Brazil’s Supreme Federal Court or contemporaneous reporting by established news organizations identifying the justice responsible. Resolution Conditions : Identify the justice who issues an order during September 2026 suspending Andrei Rodrigues from his position as Federal Police chief. If multiple qualifying orders are issued, use the earliest publicly announced order. Accepted Answer Format : The justice’s full name. If no qualifying order is issued by September 30, 2026, answer “None”.
questions.current_reasoning: Normalized to plain ASCII and sharply raised Andre Mendonca (0.24 -> 0.37) while trimming other justices after an acute August 2026 institutional crisis between Mendonca and PF chief Andrei Rodrigues (G1, CBN, O Globo Aug 6-11). Mendonca—now rapporteur of both the Banco Master and INSS fraud probes (including investigations into Lula's son Lulinha)—clashed openly with Rodrigues over PF personnel shuffles, delayed reports, and Mendonca's orders demanding raw data while barring sharing with PF superiors. Although an Aug 6 emergency meeting with the Justice Minister and AGU aimed to broker a truce, 27 PF superintendents issued a joint defense of PF autonomy during the meeting (with internal PF pushback reported Aug 11). None (0.48) remains the narrow favorite given the extreme nature of suspending a sitting PF Director-General and ongoing truce efforts, while Dias Toffoli drops (0.07 -> 0.03) since he left the Banco Master rapporteurship in February.

questions.title: What immigration status will the Trump administration seek to require for noncitizens to be included in the 2030 US census?
questions.background: The decennial US census affects representation in the House of Representatives and the allocation of federal funding. Trump has previously advocated changing which immigrants are counted.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official Department of Commerce proposal, or reliable contemporaneous reporting explicitly describing its eligibility rules for the 2030 census. Resolution Conditions : Resolve upon the administration's next formal proposal specifying eligibility for the 2030 census, provided it is published by September 30, 2026. Identify the immigration status the proposal requires noncitizens to hold to be included. Publication is sufficient; implementation or judicial approval is not required. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the required immigration status, in one to three words.
questions.current_reasoning: Major update based on leaked Department of Commerce/Census Bureau 2030 proposed residence criteria rule submitted to OMB on June 25 and obtained by Wired (Aug 8) and Talking Points Memo (Aug 11, analyzed by CityLand Aug 17 and The Nation Aug 19). The circulated draft explicitly states that only lawful permanent residents (alongside narrow humanitarian carveouts for approved asylees and approved refugees) would be counted among noncitizens, excluding undocumented immigrants as well as temporary visa holders (foreign students, H-1B workers, TPS, DACA). This strongly elevates 'Lawful permanent resident' (0.35 -> 0.65) and slashes broader categories like 'Lawful status' (0.13) and 'Lawful presence' (0.08), while remaining capped at 0.65 because the text is still an OMB review draft that could be revised or delayed prior to formal Federal Register publication.

questions.title: Which Ukrainian city away from the eastern and southern front lines will experience repeated Russian strikes on fuel stations by September 11, 2026?
questions.background: Russian attacks have repeatedly hit fuel stations near Ukraine’s eastern and southern battle lines. The spread of this targeting pattern to cities farther from the fighting would broaden its impact on civilians.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official Ukrainian municipal statements and reliable contemporaneous reporting citing local authorities. Resolution Conditions : Identify the Ukrainian city outside the eastern and southern frontline areas where Russian attacks are confirmed to have directly struck fuel stations on at least two separate days between September 1 and September 11, 2026. Reports of isolated attacks or incidental damage to nearby stations do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the city.
questions.current_reasoning: An Aug 4 NDTV/CNN report ('Russia Has A New Target In Ukraine War: Gas Stations Across Kyiv') confirms Russia's fuel-station drone campaign intensified to over 200 strikes in June-July (~3/day), heavily hitting frontline Zaporizhzhia (54 strikes in 24 days, excluded as a southern frontline city) while specifically spotlighting drone and airstrike attacks on gas stations around Kyiv as the top non-frontline target. Since the qualifying window (Sept 1-11, 2026) has not yet opened, we make a modest upward adjustment to Kyiv (0.26 -> 0.30) and trim Dnipro slightly (0.09 -> 0.08), leaving 24% across other rear cities (Lviv, Kremenchuk, Cherkasy, Vinnytsia, Kryvyi Rih) or non-occurrence.

questions.title: Who will control Yemen's Mayun Island on September 11, 2026?
questions.background: Mayun, also known as Perim, is an island in the Bab al-Mandeb Strait at the southern entrance to the Red Sea. Its location makes it strategically important for maritime traffic.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Contemporaneous reporting by The Associated Press or Al Jazeera identifying which military actor exercises territorial control over Mayun Island. Resolution Date : Resolve according to confirmed control on September 11, 2026. Territorial control means physical possession of the island, not merely a sovereignty claim or the ability to threaten nearby shipping. Accepted Answer Format : The commonly used name of the armed group, government, or coalition controlling the island.
questions.current_reasoning: Breaking Aug 19 AFP reporting (Khaleej Times, Arab News, Yemen Monitor) confirms the Houthis do not currently control the Bab al-Mandab coast or strategic Red Sea islands—explicitly termed 'government-controlled islands'—but have deployed ~2,000 fighters to Taiz/Hodeida front lines and heavily bombarded Mocha port (halting port operations after 25+ missiles) and nearby shipping (striking vessel Tihamah off Mayun Island on Aug 11) in preparation for a coastal offensive toward Bab al-Mandab amid the US-Iran Hormuz crisis. Given this confirmed mobilization, Houthi seizure probability ticks up (0.22 -> 0.25), though capturing a fortified offshore island within 23 days before taking Mocha remains difficult (~75% anti-Houthi hold). Among status-quo reporting labels used by Al Jazeera/AP, 'Yemeni government' rises (0.28 -> 0.35) and government-aligned 'National Resistance Forces' (0.06, explicitly cited by Al Jazeera on Aug 10) replaces 'United Arab Emirates' following the UAE's Jan 2026 withdrawal, with 'Saudi-led coalition' (0.18) and 'Saudi Arabia' (0.11) retaining substantial label share.
